questionsToConsider: Who should be asked for input on each person: only their manager, or also two or three colleagues and anyone they manage?
Do the skill rows match what your organisation actually reviews against for this role?
Will the employee see the answers word for word, as a summary, or only through their manager?
Do colleagues know the goals well enough to comment on them, or should that stay with the manager as it does here?
guide.howToUseResponses: Filter the responses by the employee's name and read them side by side before the review. Look for points that more than one person raises, since those carry more weight than a single comment, and note where the manager's view differs from colleagues'. Turn the work examples into specific praise and the "one thing to improve" answers into one or two development goals. Respect the sharing choice each person made when you pass their words on.
customizeSteps: Rename the skill rows to your organisation's competencies or values, and add the review period to the greeting.
Replace the name question with a dropdown of the people being reviewed this cycle if you run it for a whole team.
Send each reviewer the link a week or two before the review meeting, and remind them that examples matter more than ratings.

faqs.q: What should an employee performance survey include?
faqs.a: Progress against agreed goals, a real example of the person's work, ratings on the skills the role needs, and one specific thing that would make them more effective.

faqs.q: Who should give feedback on an employee's performance?
faqs.a: Their manager at least, and ideally a few colleagues who work with them closely. This template asks each person how they work with the employee, so their answers can be read in that light.

faqs.q: Should performance feedback from colleagues be anonymous?
faqs.a: Give people the choice. Some are more candid without their name attached, others are happy to stand behind their words. The last question lets each reviewer decide.

faqs.q: Is this the same as a self-assessment?
faqs.a: No. This survey collects other people's view of the employee. Pair it with a self-review so the conversation can compare the two.
